title: Find and install a missing shared library (cannot open shared object file)
summary: A program will not start because a library file it needs is missing from the system, and the error says 'cannot open shared object file'. This finds the missing library and installs the package that contains it.

prerequisites: The name or full path of the program that fails to start
An internet connection for the package lists (first run only)
Debian, Ubuntu and Mint: the apt-file package is installed (it is not installed by default)

steps.explain: List the libraries the program cannot find. Lines that end with 'not found' are the missing ones. This only reads the program file.

placeholders.name: APP
placeholders.description: Program name as you type it in the terminal

steps.expect: A line like 'libonig.so.5 => not found'. No output means no library is missing.

alternatives.explain: If the program is not in your PATH, give the full path to its file instead.

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: Full path to the program file

steps.explain: Download the lists of which package contains which file. Needed once before searching; the first run can take a few minutes. Fedora and Arch use the command shown in their variant.
steps.expect: Debian, Ubuntu, Mint: ends with 'Reading package lists...'. Fedora: 'Metadata cache created.' Arch: 'extra downloading...'. No error in any case.

steps.explain: Search the lists for the missing file name from step 1. The result shows the package that contains the file.

placeholders.name: LIBRARY
placeholders.description: Missing file name from the 'not found' line in step 1

steps.expect: Ubuntu, Debian, Mint: 'libonig5: /usr/lib/...' (name before the colon). Fedora and Arch: package name on the first line, without version.

steps.explain: Install the package that contains the missing file, using only its name from step 3 without a version number. Answer y when asked, but only if the list shows just that package.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Package name from step 3, without version or architecture

steps.expect: Ends with 'Setting up libonig5' (Ubuntu, Debian, Mint), 'Complete!' (Fedora) or 'installing oniguruma...' (Arch), with no error.

verify.expect: Empty output: no library is missing any more. Start the program again to confirm.

rollback.explain: Nothing to undo for the search steps. An installed package can be removed again with your package manager's remove command, but programs that need it will stop working.

warnings: Install only packages from your distribution's official repositories, taking the name from the search in step 3. Do not install a library file from a random website.
Only run step 1 on programs you trust: on some systems ldd can run the program's own code.
On Arch Linux, if the system has not been updated for a long time, update the whole system first; installing one package on an old system can break it.
Libraries are shared: removing a package can stop other programs from starting.
